altText: Map of Ghana showing migration routes and the origins of major ethnic groups such as Akan, Ewe, Ga-Adangme, Guan and Mole-Dagbani.
detailedDescription: A child-friendly classroom poster: a map of Ghana with colored arrows tracing simplified migration routes of major ethnic groups into their present-day areas. Include a Basic 3 teacher pointing to the map and learners working in groups. Keep it respectful and non-stereotypical.

altText: Illustration showing different ethnic groups in Ghana exchanging goods, forming friendships, and cooperating through alliances and intermarriage.
detailedDescription: A classroom illustration split into panels: (1) trade exchange, (2) intermarriage/family connection, (3) alliance/handshake, (4) conflict shown symbolically (no violence). Focus on benefits of exchanges and peaceful cooperation.

altText: Trade items like salt, fish, gold, kola, shea butter, pottery, cloth and iron tools displayed with cowries showing early mediums of exchange.
detailedDescription: A learning-corner table display: labelled icons of common trade items exchanged among groups, plus cowries as a medium of exchange. Add a small note card about the origin of the name 'cedi' (cowry shell). Keep it simple and child-safe.

altText: Map-and-symbol poster showing examples of conflicts and alliances among ethnic groups in Ghana with emphasis on unity and peace.
detailedDescription: A non-violent educational poster: simple Ghana map, symbols representing groups, arrows showing alliances coming together. Use labels only; no battle violence imagery.

altText: Ghana coastline map with icons showing major forts and castles and a simple comparison of a fort versus a castle.
detailedDescription: A child-friendly coastal map: Ghana coast line with location pins for forts/castles. Include a small comparison box showing 'Fort' vs 'Castle' and modern uses (tourism, education).

altText: Classroom poster showing Ghanaian entrepreneurs and their contributions such as food processing, transport, and manufacturing.
detailedDescription: A classroom poster collage: entrepreneurs represented by roles (food processing, haulage, manufacturing) with learners discussing who inspires them. Keep it modern, positive, and Ghanaian.

altText: Dramatized meeting scene where Portuguese traders form an alliance with a local chief on the Gold Coast.
detailedDescription: A respectful, child-safe dramatization: Portuguese traders meeting a Ghanaian coastal chief and elders, offering goods and forming an alliance/handshake. No weapons or slavery imagery.
